label: April 6–12
title: “Remember This Day, in Which Ye Came Out from Egypt” —  Exodus 7

items.text: God continued to demonstrate His power and give Pharaoh opportunities to accept 'that I am the Lord' and 'there is none like me in all the earth.' These continued signs confirmed the Israelites’ faith in God and strengthened their willingness to follow God’s prophet.

In every case of spiritual captivity, there truly is only one way to escape. It is only the sacrifice of Jesus Christ, the Firstborn—the blood of the Lamb without blemish—that will save us and deliver us from bondage.

Pharaoh’s heart was hard, refusing to yield to God’s will. We all have times when our hearts aren’t as soft as they should be. Pondering the consequences of Pharaoh’s hard-heartedness can help us examine the condition of our own hearts.

The Joseph Smith Translation clarifies Pharaoh’s stubbornness, emphasizing his choices. As we read about Pharaoh’s responses to the plagues, we can ask ourselves: What changes do I feel inspired to make in my own heart to be more receptive to God’s will?

The Passover ritual, commanded by the Lord, teaches us that just as He delivered the Israelites from bondage in Egypt, He can also deliver us from the bondage of sin through the Atonement of Jesus Christ.

The lamb in the Passover symbolizes Jesus Christ, the Lamb of God. His blood on the doorposts signifies His atoning sacrifice, which protects us from spiritual death and delivers us from the destroyer when we obey God’s commandments.

Unleavened bread in the Passover symbolizes purity and a new beginning, free from the corruption of sin. Eating in haste, dressed to leave, represents our urgency to escape the captivity of sin and come unto Christ.

The bitter herbs of the Passover remind us of the bitterness of sin and captivity. However, through the Atonement of Jesus Christ, we can find sweetness and freedom, experiencing a new beginning in our spiritual journey.

The Israelites were set free from physical bondage through obedience to God’s commandments during the Passover. This foreshadows our spiritual freedom from sin through faith in Jesus Christ and His redeeming power.

By identifying the symbols in the Passover, we can come unto Christ and learn how to receive the blessings of His Atonement. These symbols testify of His power to deliver us from bondage and grant us eternal life.
